title: Choking – Adult & Child over 1
summary: Encourage coughing if they can cough. If they cannot breathe, speak or cough, give back blows and abdominal thrusts.

callEmergency.headline: Call {EMERGENCY} if they cannot breathe, speak or cough
when: Severe choking: cannot breathe, speak or cough effectively
After abdominal thrusts – everyone who has had abdominal thrusts should be checked by a medical professional

steps.title: Ask: "Are you choking?"
steps.text: If they can speak, cough and breathe (mild obstruction), encourage them to keep coughing and stay with them.
points: Severe choking: cannot speak, silent or ineffective cough, cannot breathe, may clutch the throat

steps.title: Give up to 5 back blows
steps.text: Stand to the side and slightly behind. Support the chest with one hand and lean them well forward. Give up to 5 sharp blows between the shoulder blades with the heel of your hand. Check after each blow whether the obstruction has cleared.

steps.title: Give up to 5 abdominal thrusts
steps.text: Stand behind them, arms around the upper abdomen. Make a fist, place it between the navel and the bottom of the breastbone, grasp it with your other hand and pull sharply inwards and upwards. Check after each thrust.
points: Pregnant or very large casualty, or you cannot reach around: use chest thrusts instead (hands on the lower breastbone, pull sharply backwards)

steps.title: Keep alternating
steps.text: Continue alternating 5 back blows and 5 abdominal thrusts until the object comes out or they become unresponsive. Call {EMERGENCY} if not already done.

steps.title: If they become unresponsive
steps.text: Lower them carefully to the ground, call {EMERGENCY} and start CPR. Each time you open the airway to give breaths, look in the mouth and remove any object you can see.

steps.title: Afterwards
steps.text: Anyone who has had abdominal thrusts, or who has a persistent cough, difficulty swallowing or the feeling something is still stuck, must be checked by a medical professional.

doNot: Do not slap the back of someone who is coughing effectively
Do not do blind finger sweeps of the mouth
Do not give abdominal thrusts to infants under 1 year
